hero.h1: Sewer Rodding in Highland Park, IL
hero.sub: Water coming up through the basement floor drain means your main line is blocked. We show you what's clogging it on camera, then quote one flat price before we rod it clear. Our plumbers serve homeowners across Highland Park and the North Shore, 24/7.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber feeding the cable from a drum rodding machine into an outdoor sewer cleanout in a front yard

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

img.alt: Diagram showing a rodding cable fed through a cleanout access point into the main sewer line, with a cutting head clearing the blockage toward the street connection

blocks.intro: Sewer rodding fixes a blocked or clogged main line, not a minor clog. Here's how to know it's time to call:

tiles.body: Water or sewage coming up through a basement floor drain or laundry drain means your main line is blocked. Call us any time, including evenings, weekends and holidays.
If you've had your sewer rodded more than once in the past year, roots or a pipe defect are likely growing back between visits.

tiles.h3: Tried a Snake and It Didn't Work?
tiles.body: A handheld drain snake can clear a sink or tub drain, but it doesn't have the reach or cutting power to break through a main sewer line clog.
When the toilet gurgles as the washer drains, or water rises in the tub when you flush, the blockage is in the main line, not one fixture. On tree-lined streets, roots are the usual suspect.

blocks.h2: Why Highland Park Sewer Lines Need Rodding
blocks.intro: Highland Park has two things that are hard on sewer lines: older homes and big trees. Nearly half of the homes here were built before 1960, and many still have their original clay pipe.

items.body: Clay pipe comes in short sections joined end to end. Roots from ravine woods and mature street trees slip into those joints and grow into a net that catches everything else. Rodding cuts through them and restores flow fast.

In Highland Park, the homeowner owns and maintains the private sewer line from the house to the city main. A clog anywhere in that line is yours to clear, which is why a quick, accurate diagnosis matters.

If roots come back within months, [hydro jetting](/highland-park/hydro-jetting) scours the whole pipe wall clean. If the camera shows a crack or a separated joint, a [sewer repair](/highland-park/sewer-repair) is the fix that lasts. We'll tell you which one your line needs.

proof.quote: It was filled with tree roots that had found their way through the joints in the pipes. He gave us several options.

blocks.h2: Sewer Rodding Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: How often should I rod my sewer line if I have big trees?
items.preview: For older clay lines near mature trees, once a year is the standard. Heavy root problems may need every six months.
items.answer: For homes with older clay pipes or mature trees near the line, annual rodding is the standard recommendation. Homes with a history of root intrusion may benefit from rodding every six months. With so many Highland Park homes built before 1960 on tree-lined lots, a camera inspection is the best way to set the right schedule for yours. See [sewer maintenance](/highland-park/sewer-maintenance).

items.q: My basement floor drain is backing up. Is that the city's sewer?
items.preview: Usually not. Most backups start in the private line you own, from the house to the city main.
items.answer: Usually not. In Highland Park, the homeowner owns the private sewer line from the house to the city main, and most basement backups start with a blockage in that line. Stop running water, keep people away from the drain and call us any time. We'll rod the line and show you on camera what caused it.

items.q: How much does it cost to rod a sewer line in Highland Park?
items.preview: Cost depends on the blockage and how easy your cleanout is to reach. You get a flat price before we start.
items.answer: Sewer rodding costs vary depending on the severity of the blockage and how accessible your cleanout is. We give you a flat quote before any work starts, so you'll know exactly what you're paying before your tech touches a tool. If the camera inspection reveals something beyond a standard rodding job, your tech walks you through what they found and provides a separate written estimate on the spot.

items.q: What happens during a sewer rodding appointment?
items.preview: We run a camera first so you see the blockage, then rod it clear at the flat price we quoted.
items.answer: Your technician starts by running a camera through the line to see exactly what's causing the backup, roots, grease, a pipe belly, whatever it is. You see the footage before any work begins. Once you know what you're dealing with, you get a flat price for the rodding, and it doesn't change once work starts.

items.q: Will a snake unclog a sewer line?
items.preview: A professional sewer rod will clear most clogs. A handheld hardware-store snake typically won't.
items.answer: A professional-grade sewer rod (sometimes called a power snake) will clear most residential sewer line clogs. A handheld drain snake from a hardware store typically won't. It's designed for sink and tub drains, not the 4-inch or 6-inch main sewer pipe.

items.q: Do I need sewer rodding or hydro jetting?
items.preview: Rodding clears the blockage. Hydro jetting scours the whole pipe wall, which matters if buildup keeps coming back.
items.answer: Rodding breaks through roots, debris, or a clog and restores flow fast. It's the right call for a first-time backup or a line that's never been serviced. [Hydro jetting](/highland-park/hydro-jetting) scours the entire pipe wall clean, not just the blockage, so if you've had the same line rodded more than once in the past year, jetting is worth discussing with your technician.
